solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Employees stick notes here (5)

blocks.note: the people who work for an organisation
a long walking stick or rod, as a shepherd or bishop carries
a bonus third sense: the five lines on which music is written

annotation.surface: Office workers leaving sticky notes on a board.
annotation.walkthrough: There is a third sense too: 'notes here' points to the musical staff, the five lines on which notes are written. The surface of office sticky notes hides all three.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for a workforce, plus the older sense of a rod or pole.

entries.clue: Period of growth bound to restrict having millions saved (10)

indicators.note: what is saved is kept safe inside, so M sits within TIE

blocks.note: to bound is to spring, leap
to tie is to restrict
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

annotation.surface: Economic growth held back by a tight budget that must save millions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'obliged to', but 'bound' is a leap on its own. The surface's growth and millions sound like economics; the definition is the season.
annotation.definitionFit: Springtime is the season when plants grow.

entries.clue: Ingredient of Christmas pudding being blamed for poisoning (3)

definitions.note: the definition describes the asp rather than naming it

indicators.note: an ingredient is something inside a mixture, so the answer sits inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: A dodgy item in the Christmas pudding is accused of making the family ill.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the asp is the snake blamed for Cleopatra's death by poisoning.
annotation.definitionFit: Legend says Cleopatra died from an asp's venomous bite.

entries.clue: Individual needing to make contact but also putting up boundaries (6)

definitions.note: the second definition describes what a fencer does; the noun is the one doing it

blocks.note: a swordsman in the sport scores by touching the opponent
one who erects fences round a field
joins the two definitions

annotation.surface: A person who craves connection but keeps others at arm's length.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a psychological profile; both halves are literal jobs, the swordsman and the fence builder.
annotation.definitionFit: A fencer in the sport wins points by making contact with the blade, and a fencer also builds fences.

entries.clue: Piece containing extremes of emotional range (9)

indicators.note: SECTION holds the other letters inside it
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: a section is a piece
first and last letters of EmotionaL

annotation.surface: A musical work spanning every mood from one extreme to the other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Emotional range' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'range' alone, as in a range of goods.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a shop's range of goods is the choice it offers.

entries.clue: Where steps may be taken to look for eavesdropper very possibly (9)

indicators.note: an eavesdropper hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to look hard is to stare
as in 'it may well be', meaning it very possibly is

annotation.surface: Where to search for someone listening in on the stairs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps may be taken' sounds like action or walking; here the steps are literal stairs.
annotation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the shaft in a building that houses a staircase.

entries.clue: Sinuous snake sheds skin (5)

indicators.note: a word's skin is its outer letters; shedding it leaves the inside

blocks.note: to snake is to slither; SLITHER loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A snake wriggling out of its old skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb here, SLITHER, not the animal; the surface makes it a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Lithe and sinuous both describe a supple, bending body.

entries.clue: What may protect vehicle at high speed? (8)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

annotation.surface: A question about safety gear for a fast car.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is vague on purpose: a carapace is the hard shell of a crab or tortoise, which protects the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the hard shell of a crab or tortoise exists to protect the soft body inside.

entries.clue: Unable to control movements of monarch barely satisfied to stay at home (11)

indicators.note: barely means stripped bare, so KING loses its outer letters
the IN stays within CONTENT

blocks.note: at home is IN
satisfied is content
KING without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A king too content to leave home to deal with bowel problems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Movements' refers to bowel movements, not a monarch's travels.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone incontinent cannot control their bladder or bowel movements.

entries.clue: I’m opposed to that, not to cycling (4)

indicators.note: the word is cycled: its last letter moves round to the front

blocks.note: a door that is 'to' is closed, so one that is not to is OPEN; the N moves to the front

annotation.surface: A protest against a cycling ban.
annotation.walkthrough: A door pushed 'to' is shut, an idiom that makes 'not to' mean open. 'Cycling' looks like the bicycle debate.
annotation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual no, a way of saying you object.

entries.clue: Feeling guilty about social worker guards confined (9)

indicators.note: RE and ANT guard PENT by standing either side of it

blocks.note: RE means about, concerning
pent, as in pent up, means confined
an ant is a social insect and a worker

annotation.surface: Someone guilty about their social worker keeping them locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is the ant, a social insect with a worker caste, not a council employee.
annotation.definitionFit: A repentant person feels guilty about what they did.

entries.clue: Go back over right step in the wrong direction (5)

indicators.note: the word is written backwards

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a pace is a step; written backwards it is ECAP

annotation.surface: Retracing a step the wrong way.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface itself describes going back, which blurs definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: summing up the main points again means going back over them.

entries.clue: Warplane once deployed uranium-enriched device causing great damage (7,6)

indicators.note: to deploy is to arrange or spread out, so the letters are rearranged
the fodder is enriched by adding U

blocks.note: anagram fodder
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: A wartime bomber dropping an atomic bomb.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is the scene of the answer, so the definition hides in plain sight at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon is a device capable of massive destruction.

entries.clue: Doctor compared his fraternity with colleagues (11)

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A physician likening his brotherhood to his colleagues.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person at the start of the sentence; it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Comradeship is the fellow feeling between colleagues.

entries.clue: Most wicked criminal singled out (10)

indicators.note: criminal means corrupt, so the letters are corrupted

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: The worst offender being picked out from a line-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, the villain singled out; it is an adjective asking for rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the superlative of godless in the sense of sinful.

entries.clue: Book author’s dedication? (4)

blocks.note: a large, weighty volume
the two words a vain author might write on the dedication page

annotation.surface: The inscription at the front of a book.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a vain author might dedicate the book 'to me'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for a heavy volume, and read as two words it is the self-dedication 'to me'.

entries.clue: Inept force destroyed Utopian state (10)

indicators.note: what is destroyed is broken up, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An incompetent army wrecking an ideal country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Utopian state' looks like a country to be destroyed; 'state' is a condition.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect place, so a utopian state is perfection.

entries.clue: Broadcast disputed piece for some time (9)

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard, so the sound counts

blocks.note: disputed is fought; a knight is a chess piece

annotation.surface: A controversial programme item running for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is a chess piece, the knight; 'disputed' is fought over. In British speech FOUGHT and FORT sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A fortnight, two weeks, is a period of time.

entries.clue: Meet politician and clerical assistant briefly (8)

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
a verger, who helps in a church, loses the R

annotation.surface: A meeting with a politician and an office assistant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clerical' means of the clergy, not office work: a verger looks after a church.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: roads or lines coming together at a point meet there.

entries.clue: Make a world that’s fitting for US singer (10)

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Creating a world fit for an American pop star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, not a pop star. The meadowlark is a North American bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a songbird of North American grasslands, so a US singer.

entries.clue: Look around for one constructive thing to do (4)

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing the toy rather than naming it

indicators.note: LO goes around the other letters

blocks.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means look
e.g. means for example, for one

annotation.surface: Searching for something useful to do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constructive' is literal: Lego is a construction toy.
annotation.definitionFit: Building with Lego bricks is a constructive activity.

entries.clue: Virulent disease leads to extremely resilient bug (6)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: pest is an old word for plague
first and last letters of ResiliEnt, in the order written

annotation.surface: A nasty infection giving rise to a tough germ.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bug' reads as a germ in this setting; it is the verb, to annoy.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both verbs mean to annoy someone persistently.

entries.clue: Green energy company that was of a mind to store insufficient energy (13)

indicators.note: ENRON keeps the other letters stored inside it
the word falls short by its last letter

blocks.note: Enron was a US energy company that collapsed in 2001
vim, meaning energy, missing its last letter
mental means of the mind

annotation.surface: An eco-friendly power firm that was minded to hold back energy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company that was' signals a firm that no longer exists; Enron collapsed in a famous accounting scandal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: green in the political sense means concerned with protecting nature.

entries.clue: Theatrical production always sent up university dons (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means written upwards, so reversed
one word dons another as clothing, so U goes inside

blocks.note: ever means always; reversed it is REVE
U is the abbreviation for university

annotation.surface: University lecturers who are forever mocked in a student show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, and the surface leans on that; it is the verb, to put on.
annotation.definitionFit: A revue is a stage show of sketches and songs.

entries.clue: Person taking action against senior officer is powerless (4)

indicators.note: P stands for power, so the P is removed

blocks.note: SUPER, short for superintendent, loses its P

annotation.surface: Someone suing a senior officer who cannot do anything about it.
annotation.walkthrough: A super is a police superintendent, a senior officer in British police forces.
annotation.definitionFit: A suer is one who sues, taking legal action against someone.

entries.clue: Guide that woman behind you and me (5)

indicators.note: HER comes behind, after, US

blocks.note: you and me are us
that woman is her

annotation.surface: A woman leading from behind a couple.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' tells you the order: in an across answer, the woman comes after the pair of us.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: showing someone to their seat is guiding them.

entries.clue: Obtain expert on those coming first in voters’ eyes such as Greens? (9)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the following words
in an across clue, GET ABLE placed on VE means after it

blocks.clueFragment: those coming first in voters’ eyes
blocks.note: first letters of Voters' Eyes
to obtain is to get
able means skilled, expert

annotation.surface: Winning over experts on how the Green Party looks to voters.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'Greens' look like the political party; the question mark allows the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: greens such as cabbage and kale are leafy plants eaten at meals.

entries.clue: Wrap last item on the agenda up (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means written upwards, so reversed

blocks.note: AOB, any other business, closes a British meeting agenda; turned round for the answer

annotation.surface: Finishing off the last item of a meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' reads as one phrase, ending a meeting; 'Wrap' is the definition, and a feather boa is a wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: A boa is a long scarf, a wrap worn round the neck.

entries.clue: Object to drinks prior to play (9)

indicators.note: what drinks takes the other letters in

blocks.note: to resent something is to object to it
pre- means before, prior

annotation.surface: Someone who objects to drinking before a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prior to' reads as a phrase meaning before; split it, PRE for prior and 'to' as the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an actor portraying a role on stage plays it.

entries.clue: Severely criticise case of auditors mired in corruption (5)

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer letters
stuck in the mud, so AS sits inside ROT

blocks.note: rot is decay, corruption
first and last letters of AuditorS

annotation.surface: Slamming auditors caught up in a corruption scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface of an accounting scandal makes 'case' sound legal; it is the outside of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: giving someone a grilling or a harsh dressing-down.
